title.title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
title.subtitle: Claim: covering $K$ by cubes and covering the cube's polar by $K^\circ$ can differ by any constant factor in the log

plain: Count the cubes needed to cover a shape, then do the same for the 'dual' shapes: the counts can differ wildly

lines.tex: \log N(K, B_\infty) \;>\; b\,\log N(B_\infty^\circ, a^{-1} K^\circ)

beats.text: Polarity swaps bodies: the cube's polar is the cross-polytope $B_1$
Pietsch (1972): covering numbers survive polarity, up to constants in the log
Claim: for every $a, b \ge 1$ some symmetric $K$ breaks it, against the cube

steps: Build a matrix of nearly 0 and 1 entries from finite-field forms
Its rows sit far apart, so covering them takes many cubes
Yet its columns' hull has a short list: the dual count is small

achievement.label: Pietsch's entropy-duality conjecture (1972)
statement: \forall\, a, b \ge 1\ \exists K:\ \log N(K, B_\infty) > b \log N(B_\infty^\circ, a^{-1}K^\circ)
achievement.context: Before: proved when one body is an ellipsoid (Artstein–Milman–Szarek, 2004)
achievement.note: The dimension grows with $a, b$; the ellipsoid and K-convex cases stand

verify.detail: The counterexample for all $a, b \ge 1$, with $N$ the least number of translates
verify.ourCheck: We read the review of the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Polarity swaps bodies; the cube's dual is the diamond. Pietsch guessed coverings survive it.
Rows sit far apart, but the columns are easy to list: the counts split.
Claimed: they differ by any factor.

sources.ref: article, Metric-entropy duality is false in general
sources.quote: Pietsch's duality conjecture (1972), in the geometric form of Artstein-Avidan, Milman and Szarek
geometric form in Artstein-Milman-Szarek, Annals 159 (2004) (proved when one body is an ellipsoid)
for every a,b>=1 there are n and an origin-symmetric convex body K in R^n with log N(K, B_inf) > b log N(B_inf°, a^{-1} K°) (L = cube)
Dimensions grow with a,b, nothing said about fixed dimension.

sources.ref: article, Metric-entropy duality is false in general
sources.quote: it does not touch the ellipsoid or K-convex cases
